verdicts.summary: The before/after branch check does not catch an A→B→A bounce inside one lookup. The value is accepted and tagged with the wrong branch.
verdicts.scenario: 1) refreshStatus (full) takes the lock. VcsStatusBroadcaster.ts:381 reads currentBranch = A. 2) GitManager.ts:1372 statusDetailsRemote runs while HEAD is B, so the PR lookup and ahead/behind values are for B. 3) Before line 385 the user checks out A again, so currentBranch = A. 4) Line 390-391: branch === currentBranch, so the B data is returned as {branch: A, value: B's data}. 5) Line 297 accepts it because the cached local is still A.
verdicts.consequence: A's cached PR, ahead and behind show B's values until the next remote read. With automatic fetch disabled, that is only a full refresh. The local refresh does not repair it because local is already A.
verdicts.missing: Not checked: whether Effect's Cache re-inserts an in-flight pre-invalidation result after invalidate. The checkout has no node_modules, so that race cannot be read here.

verdicts.summary: The localOnly path reads `previous` before its local refresh and before taking the per-cwd lock. A remote load that finishes in between is overwritten with a null marker.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Cache is (A, PR_A). An RPC vcsRefreshStatus{localOnly} (ws.ts:2922) runs line 487 and captures previous = (A, PR_A). 2) The user checks out B before the git status call at line 488 returns, so local = B. The cache is set to (B, remote null). 3) A getStatus for B, or a full refresh, gets the lock first, reads B's PR, and caches (B, PR_B). 4) The localOnly call gets the lock. Line 493 compares previous.refName A with local.refName B, which differs, so line 497 writes {branch: B, value: null} and publishes remoteUpdated null.
verdicts.consequence: PR_B is replaced by a 'no PR' marker. getStatus (line 345) and refreshPullRequestStatus (line 533) then return null without a lookup. The marker is cleared only by a full refreshStatus or a poller pass (fetch enabled). The UI hides B's PR until then.
verdicts.missing: none. Parent code read `previous` inside the lock (diff line 1005). The unbounded lock wait and remoteStatus timeout the open question asks about are pre-existing and not added here.

verdicts.summary: The visible_effect claim that 'the next refresh or poll reloads the remote' is wrong when automatic fetch is disabled (interval zero). The discarded state is not reloaded by the poller.
verdicts.scenario: 1) Automatic fetch interval is zero, and a stream is open. The first successful poll sets needsInitialRefresh to false (line 591). 2) A branch switch lands during a getStatus remote read, so readRemoteStatus returns null (line 390-392). The cached remote becomes null (line 478/547). 3) On each later tick, line 566 returns early because needsInitialRefresh is false. Nothing re-reads. 4) Only getStatus, refreshPullRequestStatus, a full refreshStatus, or a new streamStatus subscription recovers it (line 731 sets refreshImmediately when remote is null).
verdicts.consequence: The new branch's PR, ahead and behind stay absent on an open stream until a turn-end or explicit refresh. Before this change the stale previous branch's PR stayed, so this is a narrower failure. The wording of the note is inaccurate.
verdicts.missing: none. Added hazard, not in the findings. It matches the design of the localOnly switch path, which also leaves the new branch unloaded until a full refresh.
